name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3497
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Antique bicycle in famous lane with distant object

blocks.note: Penny Lane, the Liverpool street made famous by the Beatles song
a distant object is a far thing, run together into one word

explanation.surface: An old high-wheeled bicycle spotted on a well-known street, alongside something far away.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, which gave the bicycle with its huge front wheel and tiny back wheel its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The penny-farthing is the Victorian high-wheeler, now a museum piece, so it is literally an antique bicycle.

clue.text: Pick up military shirt in a river…

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a camo top is a camouflage-pattern shirt worn by soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone buys an army shirt while out on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like buying, but in a down clue it signals reading the shirt from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the river that flows past Washington, DC, into Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: …ear conclusion of first autumn sunset

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the clue continues the ellipsis from 1 Down: read with the lost opening letter, near means nigh
the closing letter of the word first
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: An autumn sunset, carried on from the riverside scene of 1 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: The published text reads 'ear', but the wordplay needs 'near', which gives NIGH; the N appears to have been lost at the ellipsis joining this clue to 1 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the time when darkness comes at the end of the day, just as the sun goes down.

clue.text: Bush's torture lawyer who heard a call for attention

indicators.note: what is heard is judged by its sound, so the spelling may change

blocks.note: John Yoo, the Justice Department lawyer who wrote the Bush administration's memos justifying harsh interrogation
the pronoun spoken, then spelt to match the call

explanation.surface: A lawyer from the Bush era who listened to a shout for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' reads as the relative pronoun introducing the lawyer, but it is the piece that is sounded out.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoo-hoo is the sing-song cry used to attract someone's notice, so it is a call for attention.

clue.text: When eavesdropping, check off bug in operation…

blocks.note: an ant is a bug, an insect
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: Someone listening in ticks off a bug that is running.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: overheard, 'check off' is the playwright Chekhov, and the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton was the first name of Chekhov, the Russian playwright whose surname is the sound of the phrase.

clue.text: …arranging tech to look up piece of spyware (what bugs could give you)

indicators.note: arranging sets things in a new order, so these letters are reordered
in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom
only a small piece, the opening letter, is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to peer is to look
the opening letter of spyware

explanation.surface: Setting up surveillance kit to search for spyware, continuing the eavesdropping of 4 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: The bugs here are both creepy-crawlies and listening devices.
explanation.definitionFit: The creeps is a feeling of unease or revulsion, which insects or hidden microphones might both produce.

clue.text: By and by, returning Yale student greeting hosts, looking pale

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside, so one piece sits within the other
returning goes back the way it came, so everything is read from the end

blocks.note: Eli is the nickname for a Yale student, after benefactor Elihu Yale
a greeting
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: Eventually a pale Yale student comes back and says hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting holds the pale word, sits after the student, and then the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: By and by is an old-fashioned way of saying soon or after some time has passed, as is the answer.

clue.text: Complaint, for example, raised about initials on a gravestone

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something flips it to read from the bottom
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the abbreviation for exempli gratia
rest in peace, carved on headstones

explanation.surface: A grievance, say, voiced about the lettering on a headstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is an informal word for a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: City in 12 deletes article to reach legal agreement

indicators.note: to delete is to strike out, so one piece is removed from the other

blocks.note: 12 Across is a compass direction, and this is the big city of the Pacific region it names
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A city in the Pacific region strikes an article from a contract to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties who settle a lawsuit agree terms out of court, so they come to a legal agreement.

clue.text: Old vessel swapping adjacent components with one getting the blame for harbor craft

indicators.note: two neighbouring letters trade places, a minimal rearrangement of the joined pieces

blocks.note: an old tub is a slow, clumsy boat
as in scapegoat, the one who takes the blame

explanation.surface: Someone takes the blame over an old boat being used as a harbor vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Joining the two pieces gives TUBGOAT; swapping the neighbouring B and G produces TUGBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat is a small powerful vessel that pushes and tows ships in a harbor.

clue.text: Look into return of fire pit

indicators.note: a return sends something back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to fire someone is to axe them
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: Someone investigates a fire pit flaring up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire pit' reads as one object, but fire is the verb meaning dismiss and pit is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is to inspect or study it closely, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Subway ran into European capital halfway

indicators.note: going only halfway keeps the first half of the word and stops there

blocks.note: to run into someone is to meet them
the Italian capital

explanation.surface: An underground train crashed partway into a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: The metro is the usual name for an underground railway system in many cities, the same thing Americans call a subway.

clue.text: Inside shelter, worth changing direction

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other, enclosed by its letters
the letters change their order before going in

blocks.note: a nest is a bird's shelter
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Indoors, something's value shifting as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Northwest is one of the compass points, a direction midway between north and west.

clue.text: Lure of shortened cable

blocks.note: first meaning: to tempt or persuade gently
second meaning: the clipped name for coaxial cable

explanation.surface: The appeal of a trimmed length of wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to wheedle someone into something, and coax is also the everyday abbreviation for coaxial TV cable.

clue.text: Tuesday Weld's parts frequently repeated: This one is very much like another

definitions.text: This one is very much like another

indicators.note: only some letters of the name are used, and each may be used again and again

blocks.note: the opening letter of the actress's first name
her surname, each of whose letters may be used again and again

explanation.surface: A comment on the actress Tuesday Weld's roles, which seem to repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the answer (T, W, E, D, L) occurs in Tuesday Weld, the American actress; the E and D are used repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedledee is the twin of Tweedledum in Lewis Carroll, so he stands for one of two near-identical things.

clue.text: "Sink was hot" (a phrase that often precedes "boy")

blocks.note: surface reading: a quoted remark about a hot sink
setter's reading: the answer itself is read as a cryptic clue whose solution is the quoted phrase, with a basin as the sink and a final H for hot

explanation.surface: A quoted remark that a sink was hot, with an aside about a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: split the answer as WAS H BASIN and it reads like wordplay, where H stands for hot and a basin means sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is the bowl with taps for washing hands, the bathroom kind of sink.

clue.text: See 25
Protagonist in Memento, say, misconstrued as cinema

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly put together, so these letters are assembled in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The hero of a Christopher Nolan film, wrongly taken to be a movie theater.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard, hero of the film Memento, cannot form new memories, an example of someone suffering memory loss.

clue.text: Rascal gets into variegated pastels in multilayered document

indicators.note: variegated means multicoloured and mixed, so these letters are mixed up
one piece enters and sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an imp is a mischievous rascal

explanation.surface: A naughty child smears coloured chalks over a document with many layers.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript scraped and written over, keeping traces of earlier writing beneath, hence many layers.

clue.text: Bird's plunder? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: a word inside is swapped for its opposite, leaving the rest unchanged

blocks.note: taken as written; its last five letters form a word with an obvious opposite

explanation.surface: A bird's stolen hoard, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Plunder ends in UNDER; replacing that with its opposite, OVER, gives the bird. 'Bird's' is 'bird is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The plover is a wading shorebird with a short bill, often seen running along beaches.

clue.text: Missile silo's cover: something to chew over

indicators.note: a cover sits on top, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word silo
cud is the food a cow brings up to chew again

explanation.surface: A missile silo's lid is something worth pondering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chew over' suggests pondering, but here it is the literal chewing of cud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scud is a Soviet-designed ballistic missile, made famous in the 1991 Gulf War.

clue.text: Where you might find young children rejecting sexually suggestive commercial with energy

definitions.text: Where you might find young children

indicators.note: rejecting sends things back, so these words are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: racy means risqué
an ad is a commercial
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A nursery that turned down a raunchy, energetic advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Day care is supervised looking after of small children during working hours, a place to find toddlers.

clue.text: I relocated to the bottom of no mountain

indicators.text: I relocated to the bottom of
indicators.note: one letter is moved to the end of the word, a limited rearrangement spelt out in full

blocks.note: a no is a denial

explanation.surface: A self-referential remark that a letter has moved to the foot of something that is not a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No mountain' looks like a phrase meaning flat land, but 'no' is a noun, a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Denali, in Alaska, is the highest peak in North America, once officially named Mount McKinley.

clue.text: Boy rested uneasily where seafood can be found

indicators.note: resting uneasily means tossing about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy slept badly in a seaside spot known for its shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is an area of seabed where oysters grow or are farmed, a place to find shellfish.

clue.text: Genre featuring two outspoken Greek characters

indicators.note: something outspoken is said out loud, so it is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: two letters of the Greek alphabet, said one after the other

explanation.surface: A film genre with two forthright Greek people in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in a story, but here they are letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a genre of books and films about invented technology, space and the future.

clue.text: Ploy of Pentagon agency, briefly supported by a couple of generals

indicators.note: said briefly, a long name is cut down to its initials
only a couple, two, of the letters are kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: the Department of Defense, headquartered in the Pentagon
taken as written, to be cut short

explanation.surface: A trick by a defense agency, backed by two senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts the second piece underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or scheme for getting round something, a synonym for ploy.

clue.text: Poet sent back fruit to daughter adopted by icy, ghoulish family relation

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so read it from the end
ghoulish suggests something grotesquely twisted, so these letters are distorted
the adopted one is taken in by the other, ending up inside it

blocks.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
taken as written, to be rearranged
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
one's kin are one's family
a son is a relation

explanation.surface: A poet returns fruit to a daughter taken in by a cold, macabre relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights, 25 and 16. 'Icy, ghoulish family relation' suggests one creepy relative, but 'ghoulish' twists only the word before it, and 'family' and 'relation' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson, the reclusive nineteenth-century Massachusetts writer of short dash-filled lyrics, is among America's best-known poets.

clue.text: Rise unsteadily to swallow 59 potions

indicators.note: something rising unsteadily wobbles about, so these letters are jumbled
what swallows takes the other piece inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
59 in Roman numerals: L is fifty, IX is nine

explanation.surface: Someone staggers up after downing fifty-nine magic drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elixirs are magical or medicinal drinks, the stuff of alchemists and quacks, so they are potions.

clue.text: The Rev. Spooner's claimed the fourth locale in the Middle East

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

blocks.note: claimed is said, and the fourth letter of the alphabet is D, spoken dee; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner asserted ownership of the fourth something in a Middle Eastern place.
explanation.walkthrough: Said is pronounced 'sed', so swapping the S and D sounds of 'sed dee' gives 'ded see'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is the salt lake between Israel, the West Bank and Jordan, a well-known Middle Eastern location.

clue.text: Novice members repeatedly appear to be trouble

indicators.note: the word's members are its letters, and they turn up again and again

blocks.note: the word's own six letters are the only ones used, several of them more than once

explanation.surface: Beginners in a club keep turning up and causing bother.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer uses only N, O, V, I, C and E, each letter of novice; N, I, C and E recur, which 'repeatedly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An inconvenience is a bother or nuisance, so it means trouble as a noun.
